chosen.title: Engagement Over Innocence: How Companion Chatbots Turned Children Into a Growth Metric
chosen.rationale: A wave of 2026 wrongful-death and child-harm suits (Character.AI/Google sued again Aug 13, 20+ pending against OpenAI, ChatGPT's teen product launched Aug 22 under fire) has made engagement-optimized companion bots the defining accountability story of the moment — exactly Dawn's terrain of corporate capture, dark patterns, and naming who pays when a design choice becomes a body count.

Colombia One — ChatGPT for Teens Amid Wrongful-Death Lawsuits (Aug 22, 2026)

rejected_candidates.title: The Data Center Says No One Asked You: The Revolt Against AI's Infrastructure Land Grab
rejected_candidates.rationale: In 2026 nearly 150 protests across 42 states and 69–78 local moratoriums (plus New York's first hyperscale pause) have turned AI's water-and-power footprint into a live fight over local democracy and climate justice — Dawn's follow-the-money, whose-community-pays angle, and distinct from AIMA's existing carbon-ledger piece because the story here is consent and power, not kilowatts.

sources.name: TIME — Community Backlash to AI Data Centers Is Growing Across the U.S. (Jul 22, 2026)

rejected_candidates.title: Grading Their Own Homework: How AI Hiring Audits Became an Industry That Answers to No One
rejected_candidates.rationale: The 2026 Workday bias suit plus California/EEOC's shift from internal vetting to mandated independent third-party bias audits raises the question Dawn would press hardest — who audits the auditors, and does a compliance industry actually protect workers or just launder the same proxy discrimination — a fresh regulatory angle distinct from AIMA's earlier résumé-bias coverage.
